Thanks Hannah — we can take this. High-level plan follows (ops runbook draft):

1) Intake & scoping (ticket RI-6742) — verify all Customer IDs and cross-check model shard mappings.
2) Inventory step — enumerate artifacts in: prompt-logs (s3:/redwood/prompt-logs/), kv-cache shards, transient session stores, analytics exports (last 36 months).
3) Canary purge in staging — run a targeted deletion for a single shard and validate application behavior and rollback.
4) Purge job (region-by-region):
   - Schedule low-traffic window (proposed 2028-02-16 02:00 UTC)
   - Delete prompt logs + output caches + session records tied to CA-9381 using deterministic keys
   - Expire / zeroize in-memory KV caches and invalidate any cached prefixes
5) Logs and audit evidence generation: produce machine-readable manifest.csv (object path, deletion timestamp, checksum), a short human summary, and sanitized syslog snippets showing deletions.
6) Delivery: upload evidence bundle to a secure S3 share and provide signed attestation doc.

Estimated elapsed time: 48–72 hours from approval assuming no cross-region complications. Blockers: need final CustID mapping (they attached a mapping file), legal attestation format, and confirmation if CloudApps wants on-prem/private deployment artifacts included.

Attachments (for internal ops): purge-manifest.csv (template), deletion-evidence-template.docx

I'll create the RI ticket now and schedule the canary.

— Marissa Cole
Sr. Runbook Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Complete purge of CloudApps customer prompts/outputs/logs (CustID: CA-9381)

Adding a few technical notes:
- Pin model variants for the window: ensure requests are routed to the same quantization/profile so cache keys match and we avoid inconsistent states.
- Snapshot before purge: take a read-only snapshot of affected stores (immutable archive) for legal hold if required — keep for 7 days then destroy unless instructed otherwise.
- KMS/HSM: we won't rotate keys as part of the purge; zeroization applies to application-level caches. If CloudApps requires crypto-level key zeroization, that's an extra step and needs legal sign-off.
- Monitoring: will enable trace collection for the canary and first full pass to verify no upstream failures.

Agree with Marissa that 02:00 UTC on 2028-02-16 is a good slot. I will own the canary telemetry and rollback hooks.

— Rishi Malhotra
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
